## Overview

This repository contains the supplementary materials for the paper "Adaptive Bayesian Multivariate Spline Knot Inference with Prior Specifications on Model Complexity" by Junhui He, Ying Yang, and Jian Kang.

The ABMRS R package implements the methodology described in the paper and is publicly available at [https://github.com/junhuihe2000/ABMRS](https://github.com/junhuihe2000/ABMRS).
The R codes for all simulation studies and real data analyses presented in the paper are publicly available at [https://github.com/junhuihe2000/exampleABMRS](https://github.com/junhuihe2000/exampleABMRS).

## Installation

To install the ABMRS package from GitHub, execute the following commands in R:

```{r eval=FALSE}
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("junhuihe2000/ABMRS")
```

## Repository Contents

- **`ABMRS_Biometrics_Supplement.pdf`**: Detailed supplementary materials including additional simulation results, theoretical proofs, and computational details.
- **`data/`**: Real data sets analyzed in the paper, including the triceps skinfold thickness data.
- **`demo/`**: Reproducible R scripts and R Markdown files for all simulation studies and real data analyses presented in the paper.

## Illustrative Example

The following example demonstrates the application of ABMRS for knot inference in univariate linear spline regression. We simulate data from a piecewise linear function with four true knots and apply the ABMRS algorithm to recover the knot locations and their posterior distributions.

### Data Generation

```{r}
library(ABMRS)
library(splines)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggpubr)

# Define the true piecewise linear function with four knots
f = function(x) {
  knots = c(0.2, 0.2, 0.5, 0.7)
  beta = c(0, -1, 1, 0, 1, 0)
  B = bs(x, knots = knots, degree = 1, intercept = TRUE, Boundary.knots = c(0, 1))
  y = B %*% beta
  return(y)
}

# Generate simulated data
set.seed(1234)
m = 500  # Sample size
sd = 0.4  # Noise level

x = runif(m, 0, 1)
y = f(x)
y_obs = y + rnorm(m, 0, sd)  # Add Gaussian noise

# Visualize the observed data and true function
p = ggplot() + 
  geom_point(aes(x, y_obs), size = 0.6, col = "red") + 
  geom_line(aes(x, y)) + 
  theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(), axis.title.y = element_blank())

annotate_figure(p, top = "Simulated Data: Linear Splines with Four Knots")
```

### ABMRS Knot Inference

```{r}
# Apply ABMRS algorithm
ebars = ebars(x, y_obs, gamma = 1, c = 0.3, time = 2, degree = 1, intercept = TRUE)
ebars$rjmcmc(burns = 5000, steps = 5000)  # Run RJMCMC with 5000 burn-in and 5000 iterations

# Extract posterior samples of knots
knots = ebars$knots()
nums = sapply(knots, function(xi) { return(length(xi)) })
points = unlist(knots)

# Visualize posterior distributions
p1 = ggplot(mapping = aes(x = nums)) + 
  geom_bar(aes(y = after_stat(prop))) + 
  ylab("") + xlab("Number of Knots") + 
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = mean(nums)), color = "red", linetype = "dashed") + 
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(min(nums), max(nums)), 
                     labels = seq(min(nums), max(nums)))

p2 = ggplot(mapping = aes(x = points)) + 
  geom_density(adjust = 1) + 
  ylab("") + xlab("Knot Location")

annotate_figure(ggarrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2, nrow = 1, align = "hv"),
                top = "Posterior Distributions from ABMRS")
```
